requirement:
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
rationale: The tests adequately cover `requirements.test-coverage.index.details`. **Per-process detail subchapters, identifying fields, and link back** - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles]` records two tests. It asserts the index has five sub-items: the attempt details, captured sources and file notes. - That test checks every "Test process coverage" subchapter for these items: - `Binary: binary` - `Attempt: 1` - `Outcome: success` - `Captured at Unix ns` - `[Back to coverage index](../coverage.html)` - It checks that the index links to each detail page, and that the detail for test `one` shows `Test: one` and `Run: {first_run}`. - The two tests use different run ids, so run identification is distinguished. - `fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_index_hierarchy_after_existing_children]` checks that the generated pages are placed under the index chapter. It also checks their section numbering and parent names, and that each page links back to `../coverage.html`. - The attempt and outcome fields are only ever asserted with `1` and `success`, because the `record` fixture hard-codes both. The detail renderer, `fn[detail]`, writes these fields straight from the attempt data with no conditional or transformation. That is the unchanged-pass-through exemption, so I do not count it as a gap. - `fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]` covers failed and interrupted outcomes, stale coverage, and a different build configuration. Detail pages are still produced there, and the stale case checks the saved source. **Executed versus unexecuted lines, counts, and source captured for the run** - `.github/scripts/coverage-viewer.test.mjs` (the test "process reports preserve counters, source text, child identity and lazy file rendering") checks the viewer output: - counts are shown, including the extreme value `18446744073709551615 executed`, alongside `0 unexecuted`; - the captured source text is rendered literally (``); - source is accepted only from the matching frame and run. - The book test `reports_identify_attempts_...` checks that the detail embeds the counters as JSON, for example `"1":"0","2":"7"`. - The same test rewrites `code.rs` after the run. It then asserts that the saved source `fn one() {}` and the counters are still shown, and that the profile files are retained. This covers "using the source captured for that run". - `fn[rendered_detail_scripts_remain_literal_across_blank_lines]` checks that the generated detail page embeds the viewer script and the counts through markdown rendering. **Child coverage distinguishable** - The book test checks that the detail JSON contains both `"kind":"Test"` and `"kind":"Child"` process entries. The child process has its own counts (`2:7`). - The viewer test checks that the child process gets its own "Child process 2" section with its own lazily rendered source. The child's source is absent until the section is opened. I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} index.details
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
